title: Lake Ontario or Lake America? Tribal Leaders Say: Keep the Name
summary: Lake Ontario has carried its name for a very long time — long before Canada or the United States existed. Now the National Congress of American Indians is asking President Donald Trump to reverse his order renaming it Lake America. Trump directed all parts of the federal government in August to start calling the lake Lake America. The name Ontario comes from Indigenous languages. In Seneca, the lake is called sga:nyodai:yoh, meaning 'beautiful lake.' In Wendat, it is ontari:io, meaning 'the lake is beautiful, the lake is big.' The change dismayed Haudenosaunee communities on both sides of the border, whose languages are the source of the name. The National Congress of American Indians represents American Indian and Alaska Native tribal governments in the United States. It says the order shows disrespect for Indigenous geographic names and for Indigenous cultural, spiritual, and historical relationships with lands and waters. A resolution rejecting the name change was passed at the organization's October assembly. It was introduced by the Seneca Nation of Indians, a community based in western New York. The resolution says efforts to rename geography on their own risk erasing Indigenous history. It calls on the U.S. federal government to suspend its use of the term 'Lake America.' It also asks governments to preserve and respect Indigenous names, in consultation with affected Tribal Nations. Wendat Nation Grand Chief Pierre Picard told The Canadian Press his nation was 'shocked' to hear about the renaming. He called it an attempt to eradicate their history in the region. The Wendat occupied parts of the St. Lawrence Valley up to the Great Lakes, and the area was rich with trade routes before and after contact with Europeans. Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the lake remains Lake Ontario 'then, now and always.'
why_it_matters: Place names hold the history and languages of the peoples who first lived in a region. This dispute is about whether renaming a lake erases that history or respects the communities it belongs to.

background_read: Lake Ontario is one of the Great Lakes, a group of very large lakes on the border between Canada and the United States.
Indigenous peoples lived around these lakes long before Canada or the United States existed, and many place names in the region come from their languages.
Place names can carry history, language, and meaning, so changing a name can feel like losing a link to the past for the people whose language it came from.
Tribal governments represent Indigenous nations and speak for their communities on matters that affect their lands, waters, and cultures.
